# Native axis-line screen controls

Original, independently authored textless OOXML, generated by
`python tools/axis_line_display_fixture.py`. Twenty-four anchored lines cross
horizontal/vertical axes, flat/round/square caps and four fractional phases.
The 3.5pt declared pen occupies five device pixels at 100% zoom and DPR 1.

`native-screen-atlas.png` retains only the neutral authored lines from the reference
application, captured on 2026-10-05 with the unchanged owned source open,
Saved and at 100% zoom. Source, cases and crop hashes plus measured footprints
are in `native-screen-reference.json`. The full private capture is not shipped.
No font programs were read or redistributed. The fixture generator and neutral
artwork are original project test resources under the project's terms.

DrawingML line properties/caps (ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.2.2.24 and 20.1.10.31)
define flat endpoints. The prior inclusive-endpoint hypothesis is withdrawn
(2026-10-10): threshold-128 JPEG footprints pass when half-gray cap pixels are
incorrectly made black. The renderer retains the original half-pixel projection.
All 24 dark-core bounds and 80 flat-cap half-gray samples now pass. The original
threshold-128 footprint assertions remain unchanged as expected-failure
diagnostics, not a justification for extending the geometric path. Exact
endpoint alpha and broader cap fidelity remain unproven.

`tools/record_axis_line_coverage.py` reproduces the coverage references from
the retained crops. Dark cores use max(R,G,B)<96; gray samples use 96–192 with
a maximum 32-channel JPEG allowance, which rejects replacing gray by black
or white. This does not certify exact JPEG color/alpha. The paired pen fixture
adds a fresh 75% native observation. No font program from the reference application is read or shipped.

Run `python tools/check_axis_line_reference.py` to reproduce native footprints
from the retained crops. Browser tests check native footprints, source/export,
undo/reopen and unchanged physical print pixels across cache-mode switches.
Physical hashes are a main-baseline regression oracle, not native PDF equivalence.

The physical-print correction on 2026-10-10 supersedes those stored print
hashes: they captured screen-rounded widths. The browser suite now asserts
physical pen widths and print repeatability across screen cache switches.
Dashed screen hashes and all native screen assertions remain unchanged.
